about: .NET 10's answers for the Mac help keyword index (Sources/HelpKeywordIndex.swift), checked by Tests/help-keyword-index-test.swift and recomputed by Tests/HelpKeywordIndexDotNet. Tests/verification.md says how they were made.

source.method: Windows's HelpCatalog.cs and HelpIndexMenu.ApplyFilter at d783a494 as .NET runs them, with Uri.TryCreate(text, UriKind.Absolute) refusing a single leading '/', as it does on Windows. On macOS .NET uses the system's ICU, /usr/lib/libicucore.dylib.
source.strings: A string is JSON text, or an array of its UTF-16 code units where it holds U+0000, U+FEFF or an unpaired surrogate.

filter.about: HelpIndexMenu.ApplyFilter on the keyword map of help publication 7101cea6 (Content/Help/keyword-index.json, git blob 329ead83): CompareInfo.IndexOf in en-GB with IgnoreCase | IgnoreNonSpace on the term or the title, after String.Trim. map is that file's entries as [term, title, path] in a seeded shuffled order (the help builder writes them sorted), so that the sort has work to do; order is HelpCatalog.IndexEntries' order for that input as indexes into map; each query is [query, hit count] with, for at most 20 hits, the hits as indexes into that order.
filter.sample: 1153 of 6949 queries: every non-ASCII query, every query with no hit or with every entry a hit, every query the no-ICU fallback answers differently, and a seeded eighth of the rest.

ordinalAndEnglish.about: Each case is [a, b, sign of string.Compare(a, b, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase), 1 if StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase.Equals(a, b) else 0, sign of StringComparer.Create(en-GB, ignoreCase: true).Compare(a, b)], HelpCatalog's keys and its order of terms and titles.
ordinalAndEnglish.sample: 5433 of 40000 random pairs over 76 awkward characters: every pair whose OrdinalIgnoreCase answer depends on case folding (1310), every pair whose en-GB answer changes when case, width, kana type or non-spacing marks count differently (155), every pair the no-ICU fallback orders differently (271), and a seeded tenth of the rest.

uriPathAndFragment.about: Each case is [path, fragment or null, AbsolutePath.TrimStart('/'), Fragment] of new Uri("https://help.statsdirect.invalid/" + path + (fragment is null ? "" : "#" + fragment)), the form HelpCatalog.Resolve gives a topic's path and fragment.
uriPathAndFragment.sample: 5200 of 84120 cases: every case of the constructed corpora and a seeded sample of the random ones (corpus 1078 of 1078, corpus2 82 of 82, corpus3 52 of 52, corpus4 58 of 58, corpus6 200 of 200, corpus7 2156 of 2156, corpus8 46 of 46, corpus9 64 of 64, corpus11 384 of 384, corpus5 480 of 30000, corpus10 600 of 50000).

aliasAddressParts.about: Each case is [address, Host, AbsolutePath, Fragment, GetLeftPart(UriPartial.Authority), PathAndQuery] of an address Uri.TryCreate(address, UriKind.Absolute) accepts, the parts HelpCatalog.Resolve reads from an alias's link.
aliasAddressParts.sample: 1008 of 12600 realistic alias-link addresses (schemes, hosts, ports, dot segments, queries and fragments in combination), seeded.

absoluteAddresses.about: Each case is [text, 1 if Uri.TryCreate(text, UriKind.Absolute) succeeds else 0], with a single leading '/' refused as on Windows. HelpCatalog refuses a keyword target that is an absolute address.
absoluteAddresses.sample: All 231 cases: drive, UNC, file, scheme, authority and port forms, and bracketed IPv6 literals.
